correctness.rationale: The spectral theorem reduces the squared radius exactly to the angular integral of a maximum of three squared cosine profiles. A directly proved centered-arc rearrangement lemma bounds each winner cell. Jensen gives equal weak lengths and a strictly concave one-variable envelope, whose unique optimizer is L=pi-4arcsin(r/2). The explicit symmetric three-phase arrangement has exactly the corresponding centered winning arcs, proving sharpness. Strict rearrangement/Jensen equality proves phase uniqueness modulo pi and weak permutation. Algebraic expansion gives the displayed cubic onset, including the r=1 endpoint. The packaged checker independently passed 1,156 finite deterministic assertions; these do not replace the all-r proof.

originality.rationale: The full source arXiv:2610.04844v2 defines the integral radius and proves general norm inequalities, but no optimization over three prescribed spectral moduli is present. The published exact projective-gap formula for unitary spectra covers r=1 only, while prior two-point normal profiles include one weak mode only. The new conclusion concerns all independently variable phases for 0<r<1, obtains a unique global phase law, and a cubic onset. Searches of published mathematical records and prior work found no theorem with these moduli or a stronger direct implication. A historical weighted-circle theorem under different language remains the principal priority risk.
residual_risks: A historical weighted Voronoi-circle, optimal quantization, or rearrangement theorem could subsume this parameter-specific phase law under different names.
No independent publication-priority search or external mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Optimizing both phases of a normal three-point spectrum with fixed moduli 1,r,r is the first natural multi-mode fixed-magnitude case beyond the two-point spectrum. The exact M(r), unique global phase arrangement arccos(r/2), and cubic weak-mode activation quantify a real geometric interaction and interpolate between the unweighted unitary regular-triangle design and a weak-mode limit. The sharp closed result can guide spectra maximizing this newly defined integral norm and extends the known unitary endpoint to all 0<r<1; it is not an arbitrary finite numerical lookup.
